extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policymakers, donors, and the African scientific community (prospective grantees, fellows, partners)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the African Academy of Sciences' mission, mandates, and programme pillars that define its research, funding, policy, and fellowship priorities across Africa. Useful for assessing fit for collaboration, nomination, or funding alignment with AAS objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate 1 — Pursue excellence by recognizing leading scholars and achievers
rubrics_metrics.description: To pursue excellence by recognizing leading scholars and achievers. Recognizing and celebrating outstanding African scholars and professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honouring leading African scholars who shape continental progress; implied priority for activities that identify and elevate scholarly excellence (e.g., fellowship nominations, awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate 2 — Provide advisory services and act as a think-tank for STI policy
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide advisory services and act as a think-tank for shaping STI strategies and policies in Africa. Helping shape the future of science and technology policy across the continent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAS positions itself to influence policy and strategy; preference for work that generates evidence, policy recommendations, or advisory outputs that inform national or continental STI frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate 3 — Implement key STI programmes that impact development challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: To implement key Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) programmes that have an impact on challenges of development. Driving innovation and solutions to address Africa's most pressing development challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on programme delivery that translates research into real-world solutions; grant- or project-level activities should demonstrate clear pathways to development impact and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Health & Well-being
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancing biomedical, public health and clinical research that improves lives across Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes and proposals aligned to biomedical, public health, or clinical research that show potential to improve population health across African contexts are priorities under this pillar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Climate & Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Driving sustainable solutions, ecological resilience and climate adaptation research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that addresses sustainability, resilience, and adaptation to climate change (including applied research and solutions) aligns with AAS priorities in this pillar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Innovation & Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Catalysing breakthroughs in digital, engineering and emerging technologies for development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that develop or translate digital, engineering, or emerging technology innovations for development outcomes are prioritized under this pillar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Science Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Shaping evidence-based policy frameworks that anchor science at the heart of public life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities that produce evidence, policy tools, or advocacy to integrate science into public policy and governance align with this pillar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational scope and values — Pan‑African, non‑aligned, non‑political, not‑for‑profit
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAS is a non-aligned, non-political, not-for-profit Pan-African organization headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, with a hosting agreement with the government of Kenya. The AAS' vision is to see transformed lives on the African continent through science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partners, applicants, and activities should align with pan‑African reach/impact and the organization's non‑political, non‑aligned stance; recognition by and engagement with African Union and continental stakeholders is a relevant consideration for collaboration and program fit.
